subject: general
question: Which foreign constitution is the source of 'The idea of the Rule of Law' of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**UK**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The idea of the Rule of Law** in the Indian Constitution is derived from the **UK Constitution**.
 
• The concept emphasizes that all individuals and institutions are subject to and accountable to law that is fairly applied and enforced.
 
• It forms a fundamental principle of governance in a democratic society, ensuring equality before the law.
 
• The Rule of Law is crucial for the protection of individual rights and the limitation of arbitrary power.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Indian Constitution adopted various principles from different foreign constitutions to create a comprehensive and balanced legal framework.
 
• For instance, the concept of Fundamental Rights is borrowed from the USA, while the Directive Principles of State Policy are inspired by the Irish Constitution.
 
• The Rule of Law, as established in the UK, has been a guiding principle in ensuring that the law is supreme and no one is above the law in India.
 
• This principle has been upheld by the Indian judiciary to maintain the integrity and fairness of the legal system.
